gaps.uae_position: The duty is the law's own words; the operator's licence 3.2 makes it a licence condition; the instruments that would set the age signal, the caregiver check and the penalties do not exist yet (searched 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-22, both languages). Two published texts come near and neither reaches a telecom channel. Cabinet Resolution 106/2026 (issued 2026-06-17, in force 2026-06-30) 'shall apply to all Social Media Platforms whose services are made available within the State or directed at users therein' (Art 2); it lists age-verification mechanisms for those platforms (Art 4(2)) and says 'Self-declaration of age ... shall not be recognized' (Art 4(3)), but its standards are still to be 'approved by the Child Digital Safety Council upon the proposal of the Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority' (Arts 3(4)(c), 4(1)(h), 4(2)(d)) and its penalties are those 'prescribed under the list of administrative penalties issued pursuant to the provisions of the Decree by Law' (Art 7(1), 7(2)), the Art 16 list that is not published. TDRA's 'Telecom for Minors' page (consumer hub, updated 2026-10-01) describes an initiative launched 'in collaboration with licensed telecommunications service providers' that 'Supports the goals of the UAE child digital safety law'; its terms 'are determined by each service provider', the links 'are provided for consumer information only', and it is not on the TDRA Regulations and Ruling register.

gaps.uae_position: The language duty is binding and fined; Mizan meets it by answering in the subscriber's language with the clause quoted in that language. Nothing says the Arabic answer must be as good as the English one, and nothing measures it: the QoS Policy counts waits and faults, not languages. gaps.gap: A misheard or misread order: the CPR defaults an on-screen yes/no to 'no' to avoid an accidental 'yes' (4.22.3, 4.23.3), requires an OTP for each online purchase (4.23.2) and a recording of verbal consent on telephone sales (4.17.3); no text says what a voice or chat channel must do when it interprets the subscriber's words itself, so 'don't add it' heard as 'add it' reaches the OTP step without being read back.

gaps.uae_position: The CPR already knows the problem on a screen: the safe default is 'no' (4.22.3, 4.23.3) and a purchase needs a second factor (4.23.2). On a voice or chat channel the system, not the subscriber, decides what was said; the OTP then confirms that the subscriber wants something, not that the channel understood the right thing. ET 12(7) reaches transmission errors only. No published TDRA text requires the channel to state the service, price and term it understood and take a correction before the second factor.

gaps.line: the Cabinet schedule of licensee fines under Telecom Law 79 bis (2) is unpublished
